citation: Li X, Manley JL. Inactivation of the SR protein splicing factor ASF/SF2 results in genomic instability. Cell. 2005;122:365-378. doi:10.1016/j.cell.2005.06.008.
description: ASF/SF2, now SRSF1, depletion in vertebrate cells caused R-loop formation, double-strand DNA breaks, high-molecular-weight DNA fragments, and hypermutation; RNase H rescued the DNA-fragmentation and hypermutation phenotypes. This provides direct target-specific evidence that SRSF1 loss can disturb nascent RNP packaging and genome stability, but not the exact neuronal mRNA directions observed here.

citation: Li X, Niu T, Manley JL. The RNA binding protein RNPS1 alleviates ASF/SF2 depletion-induced genomic instability. RNA. 2007;13:2108-2115. doi:10.1261/rna.734407.
description: RNPS1 overexpression suppressed DNA fragmentation, hypermutation, and G2 arrest in ASF/SF2-depleted cells, supporting a model in which SRSF1 and other RNA-binding proteins assemble nascent RNPs that prevent transcriptional R-loops. This connects SRSF1 loss to an RBP-buffered RNA-processing stress mechanism rather than to a specific signed abundance change in the Perturb-seq genes.

citation: Olazabal-Herrero A, He B, Kwon Y, Gupta AK, Dutta A, Huang Y, Boddu P, Liang Z, Liang F, Teng Y, Lan L, Chen X, Pei H, Pillai MM, Sung P, Kupfer GM. The FANCI/FANCD2 complex links DNA damage response to R-loop regulation through SRSF1-mediated mRNA export. Cell Reports. 2024;43:113610. doi:10.1016/j.celrep.2023.113610.
description: This study showed that SRSF1 interacts with FANCD2, promotes assembly of the SRSF1-NXF1 mRNA-export complex, and suppresses R-loop accumulation. It supplies a target-specific bridge from SRSF1 to mRNA export and R-loop avoidance that is relevant to an RNA-processing response but remains upstream of the observed mRNA program.

citation: Sun S, Zhang Z, Sinha R, Karni R, Krainer AR. SF2/ASF autoregulation involves multiple layers of post-transcriptional and translational control. Nature Structural & Molecular Biology. 2010;17:306-312. doi:10.1038/nsmb.1750.
description: SRSF1 was shown to negatively autoregulate through alternatively spliced, unproductive transcripts, nonsense-mediated decay, and translational repression through its ultraconserved 3-prime UTR. This documents that SRSF1 dosage is embedded in post-transcriptional feedback, a partial bridge to the recurrent RNA-regulatory module in the screen.

citation: Sun L, Lv Z, Chen X, Ye R, Tian S, Wang C, Xie X, Yan L, Yao X, Shao Y, Cui S, Chen J, Liu J. Splicing factor SRSF1 is essential for homing of precursor spermatogonial stem cells in mice. eLife. 2024;13:e89316. doi:10.7554/eLife.89316.
description: Mouse germ-cell Srsf1 deletion altered gene expression and splicing, LACE-seq detected SRSF1-bound RNAs, and SRSF1 physically associated with RNA-splicing proteins including SART1, RBM15, and SRSF10. The work transfers the SRSF1 RNA-processing role to mouse loss of function, but in germ cells rather than postmitotic neurons.

citation: Karni R, Hippo Y, Lowe SW, Krainer AR. The splicing-factor oncoprotein SF2/ASF activates mTORC1. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America. 2008;105:15323-15327. doi:10.1073/pnas.0801376105.
description: SF2/ASF overexpression activated mTORC1, and mTORC1 activity was required for SF2/ASF-driven transformation. This is a target-specific but indirect bridge from SRSF1 to translation/growth signaling that may be adjacent to the amino-acid and integrated-stress-response genes induced in the larger Perturb-seq responses.
